claim:
Let \(X=\ell_2-\ell_1\) be the real Day--James plane
\[
\|(s,t)\|=
\begin{cases}
\sqrt{s^2+t^2},&st\ge0,\\
|s|+|t|,&st<0.
\end{cases}
\]
For Birkhoff--James orthogonality \(x\perp_B y\), define
\[
g_\perp(X)=
\inf_{\substack{x,y\in S_X\\x\perp_B y}}
\max\{\|x-y\|,\|x+y\|\}.
\]
Then
\[
g_\perp(X)=\sqrt{\frac32}.
\]
Moreover, equality occurs exactly, up to global sign change, coordinate interchange, and reversing the ordered pair, for the balanced pair
\[
\left\{
\left(\frac1{\sqrt2},\frac1{\sqrt2}\right),
\left(-\frac12,\frac12\right)
\right\}.
\]
Thus the orthogonality restriction leaves the Schäffer constant unchanged on this plane, even though the same plane has \(J_\perp(X)<J(X)\).

correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts all sphere strata. Euclidean arcs give squared endpoint norm 1+(1+r^2)/(1+r)^2>=3/2 with equality only at r=1; taxicab facets give 3/2+2sqrt(2)u+2u^2>=3/2 with equality only at u=0; axis directions from the full norming-functional segment give squared endpoint norm at least 2. The balanced pair attains both endpoint norms sqrt(3/2).
